textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 science · Materials Around Us · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: Everything around us is made of materials. An object can be made of one or many materials. Materials may come from nature, like wood and cotton, or be made by people, like plastic.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Everything around us is made of materials. An object can be made of one or many materials. Materials may come from nature, like wood and cotton, or be made by people, like plastic.
beats.speakEn: Everything around us is made of materials. An object can be made of one or many materials. Materials may come from nature, like wood and cotton, or be made by people, like plastic.

beats.en: We group materials by their properties, such as hardness, shine, transparency, and whether they float or dissolve in water. Rough or smooth, hard or soft, light or heavy are also properties.
beats.speakEn: We group materials by their properties, such as hardness, shine, transparency, and whether they float or dissolve in water. Rough or smooth, hard or soft, light or heavy are also properties.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 science · Materials Around Us · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Metals are usually hard and shiny, and they conduct heat and electricity. Transparent materials such as clear glass let us see clearly through them.

beats.en: Metals are usually hard and shiny, and they conduct heat and electricity. Transparent materials such as clear glass let us see clearly through them. Translucent materials let light through but blur details.
beats.speakEn: Metals are usually hard and shiny, and they conduct heat and electricity. Transparent materials such as clear glass let us see clearly through them. Translucent materials let light through but blur details.

beats.en: Anything that has mass and takes up space is matter. Air is matter even though we cannot see it. Like other matter, it has mass and takes up space. Solid, liquid and gas are three common states of matter.
beats.speakEn: Anything that has mass and takes up space is matter. Air is matter even though we cannot see it. Like other matter, it has mass and takes up space. Solid, liquid and gas are three common states of matter.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 science · Materials Around Us · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: We choose a material because its properties suit the use. Cooking pans are metal because metal conducts heat. Handles are plastic or wood because they do not conduct heat well.
